Ferna Equalizer

Settings and help

Ferna Equalizer is ready. Click its button in the toolbar (pin it from the puzzle-piece menu), turn it on and pick a preset. It shapes the sound of YouTube and any video or music on the web, in every tab.

How it works

  • 10 bands from 31 Hz (deep bass) to 16 kHz (air), ±12 dB, with a safety limiter so boosts never clip.
  • 28 presets: Pop, Rock, Classical, Jazz, Electronic, Hip-hop, Speech, Bass Boost, Vocal, Baila, Bhangra, Indian classical, Lo-fi and more. Move a slider to make it Custom, then Save preset to keep it.
  • Auto-EQ picks a genre preset for what is playing, from the page (title, description, YouTube's genre) and from the sound itself (bass and treble balance, beats, pauses typical of speech). A new genre must win twice in a row (about 8 s) before the sound changes, so it does not jump around.
  • Chrome lets a page's sound be processed only after you click or type on the page once. A video that starts by itself plays normally until then.
  • Some players stream from another site that does not allow sound processing; those are left untouched.

Keyboard

Turn on or off: Alt+Shift+Q. Auto-EQ and next preset can be given keys too: set shortcuts in Chrome.

Ferna Equalizer processes sound on your computer; nothing is recorded or sent anywhere. From Ferna Software Solutions.
